title: Keith Jarrett, singers and the end of the tape
summary: He loves Jarrett's playing and singer David Allyn, then tires; the tape ends.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I was looking through your records, which I guess is bad manners, like going through a bookcase, you've got a lot of Keith Jarrett there.
I love the way he plays. He stimulates me; he really opens the doors too. He opens them for me, baby, just the way I hope I open them for other people. This kid really is an astonishing musician.
I don't know. I haven't really heard anybody else of the players that I think are astonishing.
We haven't talked much about singers.
I don't think I know too much about singers. I haven't really worked with many of the great singers, people that I like.
Who are the ones you like?
Now I'm going to say David Allen, right?
I like the way David sings. There are some people I like, but I tell you, I'm losing strength in my head, man. I'm getting tired.
(Tape ended at this point. Interview concluded.)
